column1: # Requirements for Mica::HPACK (milestone H2.2): the decoder and encoder
# requirements of RFC 7541, the limits of the plan's section 2.5, and the

column3: The 61 static entries answer indices 1 to 61, and the encoder refers to them by full match or by name
Dynamic entries follow the static table, newest first at index 62; index 0 and an index past both tables are decoding errors
An entry's size is its name and value bytes plus 32
A dynamic table size update over the advertised maximum is a decoding error
After the advertised maximum drops below the table's size, the next block must start with a size update; the encoder sends the smallest size first when the maximum went down and up again
Lowering the table size evicts the oldest entries until the table fits
Adding an entry evicts the oldest entries first; an entry larger than the maximum empties the table and is not added
Integers with 5- to 8-bit prefixes encode and decode, including the C.1 examples
An integer with more than 5 continuation octets or a value over 2^31-1 raises IntegerOverflowError
String literals decode raw and Huffman-coded; the encoder Huffman-codes a string only when that is shorter
A Huffman string that contains the EOS symbol raises HuffmanError
Padding longer than 7 bits, or padding that is not the most significant bits of EOS (all ones), raises HuffmanError
Every one of the 256 octets Huffman-codes and decodes back, alone and in random strings
An indexed field reproduces the table entry
A literal with incremental indexing, with an indexed or a new name, is emitted and added to the dynamic table
A literal without indexing is emitted and leaves the table unchanged

A never-indexed literal is emitted marked never_indexed and leaves the table unchanged; the encoder sends cookie, set-cookie, authorization, proxy-authorization and fields marked never_indexed this way
A dynamic table size update after the first field of a block is a decoding error
Every example of C.2 to C.6 decodes to its headers and table, and the encoder reproduces its bytes
Every story in every implementation directory decodes, case by case in one context, to the expected headers; the archive's sha256 is checked
The encoder's blocks for every raw-data story, and for random header lists with table size changes, decode to the lists given (nghttp2 decodes them too: fuzz/hpack_nghttp2)
The same header lists in the same order give the same bytes
A block whose decoded list passes max_header_list_bytes (an HPACK bomb) yields only fields within the limit, raises DecodeLimitError, and leaves the table usable
A block over max_header_block_bytes raises DecodeLimitError before it is read
Decoding is charged to a Core::WorkBudget and raises WorkBudgetExceededError past it
A block cut inside an integer or a string raises TruncatedBlockError
After a decoding error the decoder refuses later blocks
Random and mutated blocks only raise Mica errors and allocate in proportion to the block
